result.title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders
result.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables, and 14 pages of Supplementary Material with 8 figures
result.summary: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our findings identify a shared off-manifold failure mode of modern vision encoders and suggest sparse blank-canvas optimization as a simple probe of representation geometry.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPOOK：在空白画布上做稀疏像素级 hill-climbing 黑盒优化，检验这类视觉上无自然语义的输入能否在 OpenCLIP 与 DINOv3 中定向检索到指定类别或原型，并报告二者共享的 off-manifold 失效模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「黑盒定向优化＋语义盆地命中」探针可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正承载目标视觉语义、以及离流形表示的可靠性，但与原论文推理任务的对应关系仍需人工确认。
